Actually `f';tag={tag}'` is an f-string only if f immediately precedes quote. Here `return f';tag={tag}'` -> it IS an f-string literal! Because `f'...'`. The f is the prefix, not the variable. So it returns ';tag=t'. Oops, so mkfrom returns only ';tag=t', losing the URI. That's harness bug, not main bug. Because the parameter named f conflicts visually. Let me fix mkfrom to `return f + ';tag=' + tag`.

So all those std tests were broken. Let me fix harness and rerun.
